controlled_change: Keep exact Q8 codes and BF16 metadata in a bounded shared target/draft row cache; gather copies into Metal buffers and use the existing embedding kernel.
correctness: Ten real-table cases exercise duplicates, vocabulary endpoints, 128-row batches, eviction before GPU submission, failed-read publication and owner destruction. Nine full-model row logits and serial persistent states match. 525 Python tests pass.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Remove 642.15625MiB from planned memory after a fixed 2MiB host cache allowance, at unchanged 1460/32 expert slots.
hypothesis: Serving only requested input-embedding rows can lower constant model memory without changing quantization or arithmetic.
limitations: Experimental C++/Metal producer; production remains unpromoted.
Real MTP generation, rejection at width eight, long context and sustained coding remain unqualified.
outcome: The memory-plan reduction is 673349632 bytes. Serial validation physical peak is about 641.6MiB lower, but both compared validation runs contain startup compression. Fresh normal verifier runs with streamed rows are clean at about 9.05GiB. No normal MTP speed or paired memory improvement is claimed.
smallest_experiment: Validate streamed embeddings in the existing real-MTP width 1/4 producer, comparing proposals, all logits, persistent state and request memory at unchanged cache capacity.
